subject: Scope & authority for holding post-incident artifacts — next steps
messages:
From: Lucille Grant <lucille@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, acme-security@acmehealth.com

Subject: Scope & authority for holding post-incident artifacts

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the quick response during Monday's auth-failure incident. Our security team would like to confirm a few practical items so we can close our side of the post-incident review:

1) Minimum hold window: we need to know how long Redwood will preserve the raw request logs and any incident-specific slices for forensics/e-discovery. Please give a recommended default and the process to request an extension.

2) Ownership & deletion authority: who at Redwood can sign off to permanently delete incident slices if ACME asks for a purge after our internal review? We need a designated contact or role and the steps you'll take (audit log entry, confirmation token).

3) Access controls: we need assurance that only a small set of personnel can access the held artifacts (read-only vs download). Can you outline RBAC and temporary access workflow?

I attached a CSV with the fields we anticipate needing copied out (timestamps, request ids, client IP ranges). We may also request a chain-of-custody stub for legal—would you be able to accept our template or produce your own?

Appreciate a short response (bullets are fine) so we can finish the post-incident memo.

Best,
Lucille
Lucille Grant
Sr. Security Ops Manager
Acme Health

Attachments: acme_incident_scoped_entities.csv (csv, 12 KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lucille Grant <lucille@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scope & authority for holding post-incident artifacts

Hi Lucille — thanks for the clear ask and for the csv. High level answers below; happy to jump on a 20-min call if you'd prefer to walk through.

1) Minimum hold window
- Default: raw ingestion logs and full request traces are retained for 90 days post-incident by default for hosted customers.
- Incident slices (curated extracts containing only incident-relevant tokens/metadata) are held for 365 days unless a legal hold alters the timeframe.
- Extension: submit a hold-extension request via the shared Drive link or send a signed request to security-legal@redwood.com; extensions are approved by Security + Legal (SLA 3 business days).

2) Ownership & deletion authority
- Deletion approval: the authorized approvers are (a) Head of Security (Karthik Iyer) OR (b) VP Legal (Evelyn Hart). Karthik and Evelyn are CC'd here.
- Deletion process: 1) request ticket logged (HS- ID), 2) data slice verified against scope, 3) approver signs deletion token, 4) deletion executed and an immutable audit record created and shared with the requester.

3) Access controls
- RBAC: only Security Engineering and a designated Forensics rotation have read access to preserved artifacts.
- Temporary access: time-limited access can be granted via a just-in-time (JIT) workflow; every JIT grant requires a business justification and is logged with a ticket id.
- Downloads: exports are disabled by default; we can enable exports for legal teams under a supervised process (SLA: 2 business days).

Attachments accepted: chain_of_custody_template.pdf is fine — we can sign and return a completed copy. I attached our internal chain-of-custody template for your review (same format, added Redwood signature block).

Next steps: please confirm that the CSV columns match what you need and whether you'd like Redwood to produce the incident slices or have ACME produce them from a raw export. If ACME prefers us to produce slices, we'll need the list of request_ids / time ranges.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance PM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: chain_of_custody_template.pdf (stub, 48 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scope & authority for holding post-incident artifacts

Lucille / Neha — quick clarification from legal & ops side:

- Chain of custody: we will accept ACME's template but require Redwood to sign and add our verification entries. I attached a short checklist we'll use during evidence handoff.
- Deletion authority: confirming Neha's note — deletion requires sign-off from me or Evelyn. For clarity, legal will require an email thread that explicitly states the scope to delete (IDs + time ranges) and an HS ticket reference before any irreversible action.
- Retention tiers suggestion (recommended default):
  * Tier A (raw logs): 90 days — used for spike/correlation; not normally provided to external auditors unless subpoenaed.
  * Tier B (incident slices / enriched artifacts): 365 days — provided for customer post-mortems and audits; subject to redaction controls.
  * Tier C (legal escrow / preserved upon subpoena): indefinite until release order.

Operational notes:
- We will generate a tamper-evident deletion report for every purge and store it in our immutable audit store for 7 years.
- If ACME requests Redwood to produce the incident slices, please provide a prioritized list of request_ids and a preferred delivery method (Drive link vs secured sftp).

Karthik
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
